original_claim: ASEAN road freight market $119.43B (Mordor Intelligence, 2024 figure)
research_summary: Extensive search across ADB, World Bank, ASEAN Secretariat, ITF/OECD, national statistics offices (BPS Indonesia, Thailand NESDB, Malaysia DOSM), and Tier-1 consulting firms found NO independent government or multilateral source that publishes an ASEAN road freight market revenue figure in USD. The ITF-OECD Southeast Asia Transport Outlook (2022, OECD Publishing No.103) measures freight only in tonne-kilometres, not monetary value. World Bank LPI 2023 covers performance indices, not market size. The $119.43B figure is a Mordor Intelligence proprietary model estimate; Research and Markets resells the identical figure. A separate bottom-up triangulation using independently modeled country-level figures (Mordor: Indonesia $53.68B at 44.95% share; Thailand $21.63B; Malaysia $8.60B; remainder $35.52B for Vietnam, Philippines, Singapore, others) yields an implied range of $115-$123B, which brackets the $119.43B estimate tightly. IMARC Group independently estimates the broader SEA logistics market at $223.6B (2025), with road freight as the dominant mode — consistent directionally. The claim year requires clarification: Mordor's base year is 2025, not 2024.

new_evidence.finding: ITF Southeast Asia Transport Outlook (2022) measures SEA road freight at 771 billion tonne-kilometres (2015 baseline), growing to 2.10-2.63 trillion tonne-km by 2050. Road freight = 7-9.4% of non-urban tonne-km but 45-60% of freight emissions. No USD revenue market size provided.
new_evidence.note: ITF is an OECD-integrated intergovernmental body. This is a Tier-1 source confirming road freight dominance by emissions/activity, but does not publish market revenue figures.

new_evidence.finding: World Bank Logistics Performance Index 2023 covers 139 countries including all ASEAN members. Singapore ranks 1st globally (4.3 LPI score); Malaysia 31st; Thailand 37th; Philippines 47th; Vietnam 50th; Indonesia 63rd. LPI measures logistics capability, not market size in USD.
new_evidence.note: Tier-1 World Bank source. Confirms ASEAN logistics market is large and growing, but does not provide road freight revenue market size.

new_evidence.finding: Mordor Intelligence confirms $119.43B base year is 2025 (not 2024 as referenced in Stage 1 files). Methodology is proprietary four-step model using GDP distribution, trade statistics, fleet data, and manufacturing output. Primary sources not disclosed. Projection: $160.11B by 2030 at 6.04% CAGR.
new_evidence.note: Tier-3 source. Base year corrected to 2025. Research and Markets resells identical data — not an independent cross-check.

new_evidence.finding: Krungsri Bank (Thailand) independent industry research: Road transport = ~80% of all domestic freight volume in Thailand (2022 data). Fleet: 1.2M trucks registered end-2023, 420K commercial. 2023 goods volume growth: +1.6%. Growth forecast 2024-2026: 2-3% CAGR. No USD revenue figure stated.
new_evidence.note: Published by Krungsri Research (Bank of Ayudhya / MUFG subsidiary). Tier-2 secondary source. Corroborates market structure and road freight dominance; does not contradict Mordor sizing.

new_evidence.finding: IMARC Group independently estimates Southeast Asia logistics market at USD 223.6B in 2025 (CAGR 5.43% to $360B by 2034). Roadways is cited as dominant mode. If road freight is ~53% of total (consistent with Mordor's road/non-road split in broader ASEAN), implied road freight = ~$118-$120B — consistent with Mordor's $119.43B.
new_evidence.note: IMARC is independently modeled from Mordor. The implied back-calculation from IMARC's broader logistics figure corroborates the $119B order of magnitude.

new_evidence.finding: Bottom-up country triangulation from separately modeled country estimates: Indonesia $53.68B (44.95% share per Mordor), Thailand $21.63B, Malaysia $8.60B, subtotal $83.91B. Implied Vietnam + Philippines + Singapore + others = $35.52B, consistent with Vietnam's high CAGR trajectory. Bottom-up range: $115-$123B brackets $119.43B.
new_evidence.note: Triangulation exercise. Country reports are separate Mordor models — not fully independent methodologies, but separate calibration points.

new_evidence.finding: BPS Indonesia Land Transportation Statistics 2023 (official) covers road length, vehicle counts, traffic accidents, freight tonnage volume (230.7M tons Jan-Aug 2023, +9.78% YoY), but does NOT publish monetary road freight market revenue in USD or IDR.
new_evidence.note: Tier-1 official government source. Confirms road freight activity growth but no monetary market size.

new_evidence.finding: ASEAN Secretariat Statistical Yearbook 2023 contains transport and trade statistics including merchandise trade by mode of transport for 2021-2022. Does not appear to publish road freight market revenue in USD.
new_evidence.note: Tier-1 ASEAN official source. Transport chapter available but focuses on physical/tonnage indicators, not market revenue.

revised_claim: ASEAN road freight market: estimated $115–$125B (base year 2025). The most frequently cited figure is $119.43B (Mordor Intelligence, 2025 base year — note original claim misstated as 2024). No government or multilateral source publishes a USD market size for ASEAN road freight revenue; all sizing relies on proprietary commercial models. Mordor's figure is internally consistent: bottom-up country triangulation (Indonesia ~$53.7B at 44.95% share, Thailand ~$21.6B, Malaysia ~$8.6B, plus Vietnam/Philippines/Singapore/others ~$35.5B) implies a $115–$123B range. IMARC Group's independently modeled broader SEA logistics market ($223.6B) implies ~$118-$120B road freight component at ~53% modal share. The $119B order of magnitude is plausible and consistent across multiple commercial estimates, but cannot be validated against a primary government or multilateral source. Treat as a well-supported commercial estimate with ±5% model uncertainty.
assumption_note: No Tier-1 primary source (government, multilateral, or development bank) publishes a USD road freight market revenue figure for ASEAN. The $119B figure remains a commercial model estimate. The base year is 2025, not 2024 as originally cited. The claim should be presented as 'estimated ~$115-$125B (2025, commercial estimates)' rather than a precise single figure.
year_correction: Original claim cited '2024 figure' — Mordor Intelligence base year is 2025. At 6.04% CAGR, the implied 2024 figure would be approximately $112-$113B.

country_breakdown_if_available.Vietnam: Not explicitly stated; implied ~$14-$16B based on residual calculation and 6.40% CAGR trajectory (Mordor Intelligence)
country_breakdown_if_available.Singapore: Minimal road freight market; logistics sector GDP ~SGD 43.5B ($33B USD) total (Statista/DOS)
country_breakdown_if_available.Others_ASEAN: Brunei, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar combined implied ~$3-5B

confidence_spread.central_estimate: $119B (Mordor Intelligence 2025 base, corroborated by IMARC back-calculation)
confidence_spread.confidence_level: Medium — commercially corroborated but no Tier-1 primary validation possible
